magisterium.assessment_en: In its central message, the passage is mostly in alignment with the Catholic faith: the proclamation of Jesus Christ and the confession of His lordship correspond to the Epistle to the Philippians. Still, the claim that the events of today show the conclusion of a biblical era goes beyond what can be reliably deduced from the general signs of the times.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The quoted confession that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father directly corresponds to Phil 2:10–11 and expresses the core of the Christian faith. Christian anticipation of the end should therefore be directed toward Christ and faithful living of the Gospel, rather than toward determining timelines; upheavals can call for vigilance, but do not provide a reliable calendar of the last events.
concerns_en: The description of the present as a time heralending the end of a biblical era is not accompanied by proof and can encourage an exaggerated eschatological interpretation of current events. Church teaching warns that Christ did not reveal a chronological date of the end and that upheavals are merely the beginning of sorrows, not secure proof that the end is imminent.

sections.subtitle_en: Signs of the times and preparation through the proclamation of Christ
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about spiritual signs of the times and a time of great turmoil
sections.content_en:
Grebenar describes the present day as a **"time of great turmoil"** that is "seen with one's own eyes" and "felt." Using a comparison from the Gospel, he explains that there are **spiritual signs of the times**, similar to those in the sky by which one knows when rain will fall or when dawn will break. What is happening in the world today, according to his interpretation, indicates that a biblical era is coming to an end, and God is preparing the faithful for it.

The host sees the main preparation in one thing: **in the proclamation of Jesus Christ, the Son of God**. "This is so essential," he emphasizes. With that, he returns to the reading from the Epistle to the Philippians and again stresses that at the name of Jesus every knee shall bend and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father.

sections.subtitle: „Nema drugih puteva spasenja“: što je s onima kojima Krist nije naviješten
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar odlučno naglašava da je ime Isusa Krista jedini put spasenja
sections.content:
Iz čitanja Grebenar izvodi najoštriju poruku tumačenja: **„Nema drugih puteva spasenja. Samo ime Isus Krist je put za spas, za vječnost.“** Herezom naziva tvrdnju da se ljudi mogu spasiti po drugim religijama. Spasenje, kaže, imaju oni koji priznaju da je Isus Krist Gospodin i Sin Božji te prignu koljeno na njegovo ime pred križem.

Pozivajući se na Isusove riječi iz Svetoga pisma, više puta ponavlja da nema spasenja za onoga tko ne povjeruje u **„jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega“**.

Odmah zatim otvara teže pitanje: što je s ljudima koji umiru **u zabludi i neznanju**, jer im Krista nikad nitko nije navijestio? Kao primjere navodi hinduse, budiste i muslimane. Za njih iznosi osobno uvjerenje: **Bog je pravedan**, pa vjeruje da će mnogim takvim ljudima, osobito onima koji su „po naravi dobri“, **Isus biti naviješten prije posljednjeg suda**.

Kao uzor navodi Kristov silazak nad pakao nakon smrti na križu, kada je, prema njegovu tumačenju, navijestio evanđelje dušama prije uskrsnuća. Na sličan način evanđelje bi moralo biti naviješteno i danas. Kako će se to dogoditi, otvoreno priznaje da ne zna: možda će to učiniti sam Isus, možda sveci ili anđeli.

Kao mogući način navodi ono što je čitao o jednom svećeniku sa stigmama: njemu u snu dolaze duše muslimana da ih ispovjedi i da im navijesti evanđelje. Grebenar pretpostavlja da bi danas mnogi svećenici diljem Katoličke Crkve mogli imati tu milost i navještati „u jednom duhovnom prostranstvu“. Zaključuje da evanđelje mora biti naviješteno svakome, kako bi svatko sam odlučio hoće li se prignuti na ime Isusovo. Tko to ne želi, kaže, to je njegov izbor i neće se spasiti.

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno je ispovjediti da je Isus Krist jedini Spasitelj i da spasenje svakoga čovjeka dolazi po njegovu djelu; ipak, tvrdnja da se može spasiti samo onaj tko izričito ispovjedi Krista i prigne koljeno njegovu imenu zanemaruje katolički nauk da Kristova milost može doseći i one koji bez vlastite krivnje nisu upoznali evanđelje. Mogućnost da se evanđelje nakon smrti posebno naviješta dušama iznesena je kao nagađanje, a ne kao utvrđen crkveni nauk.
concerns: Izričita vjera u Krista nije jedini način na koji osoba može primiti spasenjsku milost: Crkva uči da Duh Sveti, po Kristovoj žrtvi i u tajanstvenom odnosu prema Crkvi, može djelovati i u onima koji nisu upoznali evanđelje, uz njihovu slobodnu suradnju.

Tvrdnja da Bog mora svakome osobno navijestiti evanđelje nakon smrti, odnosno da će se takav navještaj dogoditi prije suda, nije potvrđena kao katolički nauk u dostupnim izvorima; ne treba je predstavljati kao nužan dio spasenja.
Izraz „oni koji su po naravi dobri“ može zamagliti da spasenje nije samostalna nagrada za ljudsku dobrotu, nego milost koja dolazi od Krista i na koju čovjek slobodno odgovara.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera istodobno drži da je Krist jedini posrednik spasenja i da je Božja spasenjska volja univerzalna: nekršćani se ne spašavaju nekim drugim, neovisnim putem, ali mogu primiti Kristovu milost bez vidljivog članstva u Crkvi ili izričitog poznavanja evanđelja. Zato je Crkva pozvana naviještati Krista svima, ne pretpostavljajući ni da su pripadnici drugih religija nužno izgubljeni ni da je njihovo spasenje zajamčeno.

magisterium.assessment_en: It is right to profess that Jesus Christ is the only Savior and that the salvation of every person comes through His work; nevertheless, the claim that only those who explicitly confess Christ and bend their knee to His name can be saved overlooks Catholic teaching that Christ's grace can also reach those who through no fault of their own have not known the gospel. The possibility that the gospel is specially proclaimed to souls after death is presented as speculation, and not as established Church teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic faith holds simultaneously that Christ is the unique mediator of salvation and that God's salvific will is universal: non-Christians are not saved by some other, independent path, but they can receive Christ's grace without visible membership in the Church or explicit knowledge of the gospel. Therefore, the Church is called to proclaim Christ to everyone, assuming neither that members of other religions are necessarily lost nor that their salvation is guaranteed.
concerns_en: Explicit faith in Christ is not the only way a person can receive salvific grace: the Church teaches that the Holy Spirit, through Christ's sacrifice and in a mysterious relationship to the Church, can act also in those who have not known the gospel, along with their free cooperation.

The claim that God must personally proclaim the gospel to everyone after death, or that such a proclamation will occur before judgment, is not confirmed as Catholic doctrine in available sources; it should not be presented as a necessary part of salvation.
The phrase "those who are good by nature" can obscure that salvation is not an independent reward for human goodness, but a grace that comes from Christ and to which man freely responds.

sections.subtitle_en: "There are no other ways of salvation": what about those to whom Christ has not been proclaimed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar resolutely emphasizes that the name of Jesus Christ is the only way of salvation
sections.content_en:
From the reading, Grebenar derives the sharpest message of the interpretation: **"There are no other ways of salvation. Only the name of Jesus Christ is the way to salvation, to eternity."** He calls a heresy the assertion that people can be saved through other religions. Salvation, he says, belongs to those who confess that Jesus Christ is Lord and the Son of God and bend the knee at his name before the cross.

Referring to the words of Jesus from Holy Scripture, he repeats several times that there is no salvation for anyone who does not believe in the **"only begotten Son of God"**.

Immediately after that, he opens a harder question: what about people who die **in error and ignorance**, because no one has ever proclaimed Christ to them? As examples, he cites Hindus, Buddhists, and Muslims. For them, he presents a personal conviction: **God is just**, so he believes that to many such people, especially those who are "by nature good," **Jesus will be proclaimed before the final judgment**.

As a model, he cites Christ's descent into hell after his death on the cross, when, according to his interpretation, he proclaimed the Gospel to souls before the resurrection. In a similar manner, the Gospel would have to be proclaimed today as well. How that will happen, he openly admits that he does not know: perhaps Jesus himself will do it, perhaps saints or angels.

As a possible way, he mentions what he read about a priest with stigmata: souls of Muslims come to him in dreams to confess them and to proclaim the Gospel to them. Grebenar assumes that today many priests throughout the Catholic Church could have that grace and proclaim "in a spiritual expanse." He concludes that the Gospel must be proclaimed to everyone, so that everyone may decide for oneself whether to bend before the name of Jesus. Whoever does not want that, he says, that is one's choice and one will not be saved.

sections.subtitle: Psalam pisan „tisuću godina unaprijed“ i uvjeti zajedništva s drugim religijama
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava da zajedničke aktivnosti s drugim religijama traže priznanje Krista kao preduvjet
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim čita psalam dana: „Siromasi će jesti i nasititi se“, „spomenut će se i Gospodinu vratiti svi krajevi zemlje“, „pred njim će ničice pasti sve obitelji pogana“, „njemu će se jedinom klanjati svi velikani zemlje“, a o Gospodinu će se „pripovijedati sljedećem koljenu“.

Voditelj ističe da je psalam napisan **tisuću godina prije Krista**, a govori o onome što se tek ima dogoditi, „za tisuće godina unaprijed“. U njemu, kaže, stoji upravo ono što je i sam prethodno izložio. Žali što neki ne vide da se to ostvaruje, nego bi radije „smiksali sve religije“.

Iz toga izvodi praktično načelo za odnos s drugim religijama. Ako kršćani pozivaju pripadnike drugih religija na zajedničke molitvene aktivnosti, post ili navještaj mira, **preduvjet** je da oni prvo priznaju da je **Isus Krist Gospodin na slavu Boga Oca i Sin Božji**. Tko to prizna, smatra voditelj, sigurno će se i krstiti. Tko pak krštenje odbija unaprijed, s njim kršćani, po Grebenarovu mišljenju, nemaju što činiti i treba ga „pustiti na miru“.

Osvrće se i na aktualnu raspravu, pa podsjeća da je **papa Vojtila** pozivao druge religije da povjeruju u Isusa Krista. Danas se, upozorava, to pokušava izjednačiti, „kao eto ima i drugih ponuda“. One koji tako postupaju naziva širiteljima hereza.

magisterium.assessment: Dobro je tumačiti psalam u svjetlu Kristove univerzalne vlasti i odbaciti shvaćanje da su religije usporedni, samostalni putovi spasenja. No zahtjev da pripadnici drugih religija najprije ispovjede Krista i prihvate krštenje kako bi kršćani s njima mogli sudjelovati u bilo kakvim zajedničkim aktivnostima, kao i tvrdnja da s onima koji odbiju krštenje kršćani „nemaju što činiti“, značajno su sužavajući i ne odgovaraju katoličkom pristupu dijalogu.
concerns: Katolički nauk ne izjednačuje međureligijski dijalog ni suradnju s prihvaćanjem drugih religija kao ravnopravnih putova spasenja; kršćani mogu svjedočiti Kristu i surađivati s pripadnicima drugih religija bez uvjetovanja prethodnim obraćenjem i krštenjem.

Zajednička molitva u strogom smislu općenito se izbjegava zbog različitih shvaćanja Boga, ali u iznimnim okolnostima dopuštena je prisutnost na višereligijskom molitvenom skupu bez zajedničke molitve, uz razboritost i jasno svjedočenje vlastite vjere.
Tvrdnja da će se svatko tko prizna Isusa Krista kao Gospodina sigurno krstiti nije potkrijepljena navedenim katoličkim izvorima; ispovijedanje vjere i primanje krštenja treba razlikovati.

Psalamova slika klanjanja svih naroda može se čitati kao navještaj univerzalnog Kristova gospodstva, ali sama po sebi ne uspostavlja uvjet da se prije međureligijskog susreta mora ispovjediti kršćanska vjera.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da je Krist jedini Spasitelj i da je Crkva uobičajeno sredstvo spasenja, ali iz toga ne slijedi zabrana odnosa s pripadnicima drugih religija: dijalog može uključivati poštovanje, svjedočenje vjere i suradnju, bez relativizma ili sinkretizma. Važna je razlika između zajedničke molitve, koju treba izbjegavati, i iznimnog okupljanja na kojem sudionici mole odvojeno, a drugi su prisutni s poštovanjem.

magisterium.assessment_en: It is good to interpret the psalm in the light of Christ's universal authority and to reject the notion that religions are parallel, independent ways of salvation. But the demand that members of other religions must first confess Christ and accept baptism so that Christians could participate with them in any joint activities, as well as the claim that Christians "have nothing to do" with those who refuse baptism, are significantly restrictive and do not correspond to the Catholic approach to dialogue.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that Christ is the only Savior and that the Church is the ordinary means of salvation, but a prohibition of relations with members of other religions does not follow from this: dialogue can include respect, witness of faith, and cooperation, without relativism or syncretism. An important distinction exists between common prayer, which should be avoided, and an exceptional gathering where participants pray separately while others are respectfully present.
concerns_en: Catholic teaching does not equate interreligious dialogue or cooperation with accepting other religions as equal ways of salvation; Christians can witness to Christ and cooperate with members of other religions without making prior conversion and baptism a prerequisite condition.

Common prayer in the strict sense is generally avoided due to differing understandings of God, but in exceptional circumstances presence at a multi-religious prayer gathering without common prayer is permitted, with prudence and a clear witness of one's own faith.

The claim that everyone who acknowledges Jesus Christ as Lord will certainly be baptized is not substantiated by the cited Catholic sources; confessing faith and receiving baptism should be distinguished.

The psalm's image of all nations worshiping can be read as a proclamation of Christ's universal lordship, but does not in itself establish a condition that Christian faith must be confessed before an interreligious encounter.

sections.subtitle_en: Psalm written "a thousand years in advance" and conditions of communion with other religions
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains that joint activities with other religions require the confession of Christ as a prerequisite
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then reads the psalm of the day: "The poor shall eat and be satisfied", "all the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord", "all the families of the nations shall bow down before him", "all the great ones of the earth shall adore him alone", and of the Lord it will be "told to the coming generation".

The host emphasizes that the psalm was written **a thousand years before Christ**, and speaks of what is yet to happen, "for thousands of years in advance." In it, he says, stands precisely what he himself had previously set forth. He laments that some do not see that this is being fulfilled, but would rather "mix all religions together."

From this he derives a practical principle for relations with other religions. If Christians invite members of other religions to joint prayer activities, fasting, or the proclamation of peace, the **prerequisite** is that they first acknowledge that **Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father and the Son of God**. Whoever acknowledges this, the host believes, will surely also be baptized. Whoever rejects baptism in advance, however, with him Christians, in Grebenar's view, have nothing to do and should "leave him in peace."

He also reflects on the current discussion, recalling that **Pope Wojtyła** called other religions to believe in Jesus Christ. Today, he warns, people are trying to equate this, "as if well, there are other offers too." Those who act that way he calls spreaders of heresies.

sections.subtitle: Prispodoba o velikoj večeri: Bog kao domaćin, proroci kao sluge
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar čita i tumači prispodobu o velikoj večeri
sections.content:
Središte evanđelja dana jest **prispodoba o velikoj večeri**. Povod je uzvik jednog od Isusovih sustolnika: „Blago onomu koji bude blagovao kruh u kraljevstvu Božjem!“ Isus na to pripovijeda o čovjeku koji je priredio veliku večeru i poslao slugu da poruči uzvanicima: „Dođite, već je pripravljeno.“

Uzvanici se redom ispričavaju:

- prvi je kupio **njivu** i mora je otići pogledati,
- drugi je kupio **pet jarmova volova** i ide ih isprobati,
- treći se **oženio** i zato ne može doći.

Gnjevni domaćin tada šalje slugu na gradske trgove i ulice da dovede prosjake, sakate, slijepe i hrome. Kad sluga javi da ima još mjesta, domaćin ga šalje na putove i među ograde: **„prisili neka uđu da mi se napuni kuća“**. Prispodoba završava oštrom rečenicom: nijedan od prvotno pozvanih neće okusiti njegove večere.

Grebenar tumači da je **čovjek koji priređuje večeru Bog**, koji je pripremio veliku gozbu, slavlje i radost, ali na nju moraju doći pozvani. **Sluge su proroci** koje Bog šalje uzvanicima. Uzvanici su u prvom redu Židovi, ali danas, naglašava voditelj, i **mnogi katolici i kršćani**.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje ispravno prepoznaje gozbu kao sliku Božjega kraljevstva i ozbiljnost odbijanja Božjega poziva; tradicionalno se prvi uzvanici povezuju s Izraelom, a širenje poziva s okupljanjem drugih naroda. Ipak, sluge nije nužno ograničiti samo na proroke, a govor o „prisiljavanju” treba razumjeti kao snažno pozivanje, ne kao dopuštenje za prisilu u vjeri.
concerns: Oznaka „Židovi” može biti preširoka ako se shvati kao osuda židovskoga naroda u cjelini: prispodoba govori o prvotnim uzvanicima koji odbijaju poziv, a ne o kolektivnoj krivnji svih Židova.
Isusova riječ „prisili neka uđu” ne opravdava nasilje ili prisilno obraćenje; katolički komentar izričito razlikuje gostoljubivo nagovaranje od progona i prisile.
Sluge su protumačene kao proroci, što je moguće u okviru biblijskoga poziva Božjih glasnika, ali tumačenje ih ne bi smjelo svesti isključivo na proroke.
magisterium.enrichment: Prispodoba prikazuje Božji poziv kao dar i gozbu, ali i upozorava da se čovjek može zatvoriti pred njim zbog drugih prioriteta. Tradicionalno tumačenje povezuje poziv Izraelu s pozivom narodima, a „prisiljavanje” razumije kao ustrajno pozivanje, ne kao nasilje.

citations.document_title: In Lucae evangelium expositio liber 4 (Commentary on the Gospel of Luke, Book 4)

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation correctly recognizes the banquet as an image of the kingdom of God and the seriousness of rejecting God's call; traditionally, the first guests are associated with Israel, and the widening of the invitation with the gathering of other nations. Still, the servants need not be limited solely to prophets, and talk of "compelling" should be understood as vigorous inviting, not as permission for coercion in faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The parable presents God's call as a gift and a feast, but also warns that man can close himself off to it because of other priorities. Traditional interpretation connects the call to Israel with the call to the nations, and understands "compelling" as persistent inviting, not as violence.
concerns_en: The designation "Jews" can be too broad if understood as a condemnation of the Jewish people as a whole: the parable speaks of the original guests who refuse the invitation, not of collective guilt of all Jews.
Jesus' words "compel people to come in" do not justify violence or forced conversion; Catholic commentary explicitly distinguishes hospitable persuasion from persecution and coercion.
The servants are interpreted as prophets, which is possible within the biblical framework of God's messengers, but interpretation should not reduce them exclusively to prophets.

sections.subtitle_en: The parable of the great banquet: God as host, prophets as servants
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar reads and interprets the parable of the great banquet
sections.content_en:
The center of the Gospel of the day is the **parable of the great banquet**. The occasion is the exclamation of one of Jesus' table companions: "Blessed is the one who will dine in the kingdom of God!" To that, Jesus recounts about a man who prepared a great dinner and sent a servant to tell the invited guests: "Come, everything is already prepared."

The invited guests apologize in turn:

- the first bought a **field** and must go examine it,
- the second bought **five yoke of oxen** and is going to try them out,
- the third **got married** and therefore cannot come.

The angry host then sends the servant to the city squares and streets to bring in the beggars, the crippled, the blind, and the lame. When the servant reports that there is still room, the host sends him into the highways and hedgerows: **"compel them to come in so that my house may be filled"**. The parable ends with a sharp sentence: none of those men who were originally invited will taste of his banquet.

Grebenar interprets that the **man who prepares the banquet is God**, who prepared a great feast, celebration, and joy, but the invited must come to it. **The servants are prophets** whom God sends to the guests. The invited guests are in the first place the Jews, but today, the host emphasizes, also **many Catholics and Christians**.

sections.subtitle: Isprike današnjih vjernika: posao, karijera i obitelj kao prepreka
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj nabraja izgovore kojima se današnji vjernici ispričavaju od služenja Bogu
sections.content:
Isprike iz prispodobe Grebenar prenosi u današnje vrijeme. Danas je, kaže, potrebno otvoriti se suradnji s Gospodinom i jače „zapeti“ za kraljevstvo Božje, osobito jer **Gospa sada poziva na jaču molitvu za mir u svijetu**. Ipak, mnogi se ispričavaju: „Nemam vremena, imam posla, pokrenuo sam posao, malog ženim…“

Voditelj kaže da je takve isprike **„na svoje uši čuo“**. Ljudi bi, kaže, služili Gospodinu, prijave se u inicijativu i krenu, a onda odustaju jer „moraju ovo, moraju ono“. Takvima odgovara Isusovim riječima: tko stavi ruku na plug pa se počne osvrtati na stari život, **nije prikladan za širenje kraljevstva Božjega**.

Tri isprike iz evanđelja tumači ovako:

- **njiva i volovi** predstavljaju posao, obveze i karijeru,
- **ženidba** pokazuje da i obitelj može biti prepreka, zbog ženinih, muževih ili dječjih zahtjeva.

To što se sluga vratio domaćinu i javio da prvi pozvani ne reagiraju Grebenar povezuje s današnjim stanjem: mnogi katolici i kršćani **ne odazivaju se pozivu na obraćenje i svjedočenje za Isusa**. „Crkva se urušava, kršćanska Europa šuti“, upozorava.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na obraćenje i nepodijeljeno nasljedovanje Krista u skladu je s evanđeljem, a usporedba s rukom na plugu ispravno ističe da se učenik ne treba vraćati starom načinu života. No primjena postaje neuravnotežena ako posao, brak ili obiteljske obveze predstavljaju prepreke sam po sebi: kršćanin može tražiti Boga upravo u radu i obitelji, a specifičnu tvrdnju da Gospa sada poziva na određenu molitvu ne mogu provjeriti na temelju dostupnih izvora.
concerns: Prispodoba o velikoj večeri osuđuje izgovore kojima se odbija Božji poziv, ali ne utvrđuje, sama po sebi, da su posao, karijera ili obitelj intrinsically nespojivi sa služenjem Bogu.

Brak i obitelj mogu olla olla? The quoted source specifically says Jesus also calls to marriage and family. Framing spouse or children as obstacles without qualification risks devaluing a legitimate vocation and neglecting family duties.

Lk 9,62, the saying about the plough, is a different passage from the parable in Lk 14; its application to Christian commitment is reasonable, but should not be used to shame everyone who leaves a voluntary initiative because of work or family responsibilities.
Dostupni izvori ne potvrđuju posebnu tvrdnju da Gospa „sada” upućuje taj konkretan poziv na molitvu za mir; njezinu istinitost zato nije moguće procijeniti ovdje.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusova slika ruke na plugu upozorava na podijeljenu odanost, ali ne znači da treba zanemariti obitelj ili uobičajene dužnosti; katoličko tumačenje je izričito razlikuje od poziva da se najprije ljubi Boga iznad svega. Crkveni nauk također ističe da se Bog može tražiti u svakodnevnom radu te da je obiteljski život sam po sebi poziv i put svetosti.

citations.document_title: 17 May 1988: Holy Mass for farmers at Villarrica (Paraguay) - Homily

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to conversion and undivided following of Christ is in accordance with the gospel, and the comparison with the hand on the plow correctly emphasizes that the disciple should not return to the old way of life. But the application becomes unbalanced if work, marriage, or family obligations represent obstacles in themselves: a Christian can seek God precisely in work and family, and the specific claim that Our Lady is now calling for a particular prayer cannot be verified on the basis of available sources.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' image of the hand on the plow warns against divided loyalty, but does not mean that family or ordinary duties should be neglected; Catholic interpretation explicitly distinguishes it from the call to first love God above all else. Church teaching also emphasizes that God can be sought in daily work and that family life is in itself a vocation and path of holiness.
concerns_en: The parable of the great banquet condemns the excuses with which God's call is rejected, but does not establish, in itself, that work, career, or family are intrinsically incompatible with serving God.

Marriage and family can olla olla? The quoted source specifically says Jesus also calls to marriage and family. Framing spouse or children as obstacles without qualification risks devaluing a legitimate vocation and neglecting family duties.

Lk 9:62, the saying about the plough, is a different passage from the parable in Lk 14; its application to Christian commitment is reasonable, but should not be used to shame everyone who leaves a voluntary initiative because of work or family responsibilities.
Available sources do not confirm the specific claim that Our Lady "now" addresses that concrete call to prayer for peace; its truthfulness therefore cannot be evaluated here.

sections.subtitle_en: Excuses of today's believers: work, career, and family as an obstacle
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host lists excuses with which today's believers excuse themselves from serving God
sections.content_en:
Grebenar transfers the excuses from the parable to today's times. Today, he says, it is necessary to open up to cooperation with the Lord and pull harder for the kingdom of God, especially because **Our Lady is now calling for stronger prayer for peace in the world**. Yet, many make excuses: "I don't have time, I have work, I started a business, I'm marrying off my son…"

The host says that he has heard such excuses **"with his own ears"**. People, he says, would serve the Lord, register in the initiative and set out, and then give up because they "have to do this, have to do that." To such people he responds with Jesus' words: whoever puts a hand to the plow and starts looking back at the old life **is not fit for spreading the kingdom of God**.

He interprets the three excuses from the Gospel like this:

- **field and oxen** represent work, obligations, and career,
- **marriage** shows that family too can be an obstacle, due to the wife's, husband's, or children's demands.

The fact that the servant returned to the master and reported that the first invited do not react, Grebenar connects with today's state: many Catholics and Christians **do not respond to the call to conversion and witnessing for Jesus**. "The Church is collapsing, Christian Europe remains silent," he warns.

sections.subtitle: „Neće Europa, ima Afrika koja hoće“: poziv siromasima i poganima
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o obraćenjima u Africi kao odgovoru na nezainteresiranost Europe
sections.content:
Domaćinovu odluku da pozove prosjake, sakate, slijepe i hrome Grebenar tumači kao poziv onima **„koji ne znaju, koji nisu poučeni“**. U tome vidi objašnjenje zašto se danas mnogi obraćaju, primjerice **u Africi, gdje ljudi iz poganstva prelaze na kršćanstvo**. Poantu sažima kratko: **„Neće Europa, ima Afrika koja hoće.“**

Slugin odgovor da „još ima mjesta“ i domaćinova zapovijed „prisili neka uđu“ za voditelja znače da poziv treba nastaviti kad ga prvi pozvani, mnogi Židovi i kršćani, odbijaju. Poziv se tada širi na pogane, među koje ubraja i pripadnike afričkih tradicionalnih vjerovanja, te na sljedbenike drugih religija: muslimane, hinduse i budiste.

Grebenar vjeruje da će se mnogi od njih sada obratiti. Tako će se ispuniti riječ iz Svetoga pisma da će **mnogi posljednji biti prvi**, jer mnogi katolici i drugi kršćani, iako pozvani, jednostavno nisu zainteresirani.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje ispravno prepoznaje širenje poziva s prvotno pozvanih na pogane i naglašava da Božji poziv nadilazi granice naroda. Ipak, preširoko povezuje prispodobu s današnjim obraćenjima u Africi i drugim religijama te ne razlikuje dovoljno biblijsku poruku od predviđanja o tome tko će se obratiti.
concerns: Prispodoba upućuje na uključivanje pogana, ali sama po sebi ne potvrđuje tvrdnju da će se mnogi pripadnici pojedinih religija danas obratiti; takvo predviđanje trebalo bi iznijeti kao nadu ili mišljenje, ne kao zaključak iz teksta.
Izraz „prisili neka uđu“ ne opravdava prisilno obraćanje ni nasilje: u kršćanskom tumačenju poziv se može ustrajno upućivati, ali mora poštovati slobodu vjere.
Uopćena tvrdnja o Africi i o kršćanima koji „nisu zainteresirani“ ne proizlazi iz same prispodobe i može stvoriti pojednostavljenu sliku kontinenata i vjerskih skupina.
magisterium.enrichment: U Lukinu evanđelju odbijanje poziva otvara mjesto siromasima i hromima, a zatim i ljudima s putova; Beda to tumači kao sabiranje pogana nakon što je poziv upućen Izraelu. Katolički nauk istodobno drži da Bog želi spasenje svih ljudi po jedinstvenom posredništvu Isusa Krista, pa naviještanje treba biti univerzalno, ali ne znači da je moguće unaprijed tvrditi kako će određene skupine odgovoriti.

The Hope of Salvation for Infants Who Die without Being Baptised

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation correctly recognizes the expansion of the call from the originally invited to the Gentiles and emphasizes that God's call transcends national boundaries. However, it connects the parable too broadly with present-day conversions in Africa and other religions, and does not sufficiently distinguish the biblical message from predictions about who will convert.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Luke's gospel, the refusal of the invitation makes room for the poor and the lame, and then for people from the roads; Bede interprets this as the gathering of the Gentiles after the invitation was extended to Israel. Catholic doctrine holds at the same time that God wills the salvation of all people through the unique mediation of Jesus Christ, so proclamation must be universal, but that does not mean it is possible to claim in advance how particular groups will respond.
concerns_en: The parable points to the inclusion of the Gentiles, but does not in itself confirm the claim that many members of specific religions will convert today; such a prediction should be presented as a hope or opinion, not as a conclusion from the text.
The phrase "compel people to come in" does not justify forced conversion or violence: in Christian interpretation, the call can be insistently addressed, but must respect freedom of faith.
The generalized claim about Africa and about Christians who are "not interested" does not follow from the parable itself and can create a simplified picture of continents and religious groups.

sections.subtitle_en: "Europe won't, there is Africa that will": call to the poor and pagans
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about conversions in Africa as an answer to Europe's lack of interest
sections.content_en:
The host's decision to invite beggars, the crippled, the blind, and the lame Grebenar interprets as a call to those **"who do not know, who are untaught"**. In this he sees an explanation of why today many are converting, for example **in Africa, where people are converting from paganism to Christianity**. He summarizes the point briefly: **"Europe won't, there is Africa that will."**

The servant's reply that "there is still room" and the host's command "compel them to come in" mean for the host that the call should continue when the first invited, many Jews and Christians, reject it. The call then spreads to pagans, among whom he includes followers of traditional African beliefs, and to followers of other religions: Muslims, Hindus, and Buddhists.

Grebenar believes that many of them will convert now. Thus the word of Holy Scripture will be fulfilled that **many of the last will be first**, because many Catholics and other Christians, although invited, simply are not interested.

sections.subtitle: Kršteni su pod strožim sudom
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj upozorava da kršteni imaju veću odgovornost i stroži sud
sections.content:
Završnu rečenicu prispodobe, da nijedan od pozvanih neće okusiti domaćinove večere, Grebenar čita kao ozbiljno upozorenje vjernicima: tko **svim srcem ne surađuje s Bogom, neće se spasiti**.

Objašnjava da kršteni nose **veću obvezu, veću odgovornost i „malo stroži sud“** od onih koji nisu primili kršćanstvo. Oni koji nisu kršteni, kaže, ne mogu ni slušati ni osluškivati Božju volju na isti način. Kršteni pak imaju mogućnost svakodnevno primati sakramente, pa za njih vrijede **stroža pravila**.

Tom mišlju voditelj zaključuje tumačenje za taj dan.

magisterium.assessment: Upozorenje da kršćanska pripadnost donosi veću odgovornost uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: veće poznavanje vjere i primanje sakramenata podrazumijevaju ozbiljniji poziv na vjernost. No tvrdnja da nekršteni ne mogu slušati Božju volju na isti način, zajedno s formulacijom da se neće spasiti svatko tko ne surađuje „svim srcem“, traži važno pojašnjenje kako se ne bi zanijekali Božje djelovanje i mogućnost spasenja izvan vidljivog primanja krštenja.
concerns: Ne treba zaključiti da nekršteni ne mogu čuti Božji poziv ili odgovoriti na milost: Katolička Crkva potvrđuje nužnost sakramentalnog krštenja, ali priznaje Božju slobodu djelovanja i ne suprotstavlja sakramentalno krštenje krštenju želje ili krvi.

Izraz „svim srcem ne surađuje s Bogom, neće se spasiti“ može zvučati kao da se spasenje zaslužuje savršenom ljudskom suradnjom; treba naglasiti da je spasenje Božji dar, uz stvaran poziv čovjeka na slobodan odgovor.
Isusova završna opomena u prispodobi odnosi se na odbijanje poziva, a ne znači da će svaki krštenik biti isključen iz spasenja ili da sakramentalni pristup sam po sebi jamči spasenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Lav XIII. uči da katolici nose brojnije i važnije dužnosti od onih koji nisu dovoljno upoznati s vjerom ili za nju nisu čuli; to podupire govor o većoj odgovornosti, ali ne opravdava predstavu da Bog ne djeluje u životu nekrštenih. Krštenje je nužno i Crkva poziva sve na vjeru i sakramentalni život, dok istodobno valja čuvati nadu u Božje spasenjsko djelovanje i razumjeti osobnu suradnju kao odgovor na milost.

citations.document_title: The Hope of Salvation for Infants Who Die without Being Baptised
The Hope of Salvation for Infants Who Die without Being Baptised

citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)

magisterium.assessment_en: The warning that Christian affiliation brings greater responsibility is mostly in accordance with Catholic doctrine: greater knowledge of the faith and receiving the sacraments entail a more serious call to fidelity. However, the claim that the unbaptized cannot listen to God's will in the same way, together with the formulation that not everyone will be saved who does not cooperate "with all their heart", requires an important clarification so as not to deny God's action and the possibility of salvation outside the visible reception of baptism.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Leo XIII teaches that Catholics bear more numerous and more important duties than those who are not sufficiently acquainted with the faith or have not heard of it; this supports talk of greater responsibility, but does not justify the idea that God does not act in the lives of the unbaptized. Baptism is necessary and the Church calls everyone to faith and sacramental life, while at the same time one should preserve hope in God's saving action and understand personal cooperation as a response to grace.
concerns_en: One should not conclude that the unbaptized cannot hear God's call or respond to grace: the Catholic Church affirms the necessity of sacramental baptism, but acknowledges God's freedom of action and does not oppose sacramental baptism to baptism of desire or blood.

The phrase "does not cooperate with God with all their heart will not be saved" can sound as if salvation is earned by perfect human cooperation; it should be emphasized that salvation is a gift from God, along with a real call to man for a free response.

Jesus' closing warning in the parable refers to rejecting the invitation, and does not mean that every baptized person will be excluded from salvation or that sacramental access in itself guarantees salvation.

sections.subtitle_en: The baptized are under a stricter judgment
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host warns that the baptized have greater responsibility and a stricter judgment
sections.content_en:
The final sentence of the parable, that none of those invited will taste of the host's dinner, Grebenar reads as a serious warning to believers: whoever **does not cooperate with God with all one's heart will not be saved**.

He explains that the baptized carry a **greater obligation, greater responsibility, and a "slightly stricter judgment"** than those who have not received Christianity. Those who are not baptized, he says, cannot listen to or discern God's will in the same way. The baptized, on the other hand, have the opportunity to receive the sacraments daily, so **stricter rules** apply to them.

With that thought, the host concludes the interpretation for that day.

sections.subtitle: Promocije knjige „Isus lider“ i predstavljanje inicijative po gradovima
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar najavljuje raspored promocija knjige i predstavljanja domoljubne inicijative
sections.content:
Nakon tumačenja Grebenar najavljuje niz skupova na kojima predstavlja knjigu **„Isus lider“** i **domoljubnu inicijativu Ora et Labora**. Svaki skup počinje **u 19 sati molitvom**, nakon koje slijede promocija knjige i predstavljanje inicijative.

Raspored koji iznosi:

- **utorak, 3. studenoga**: Solin, hotel President Solin,
- **srijeda, 4. studenoga**: Imotski, Pučko otvoreno učilište Imotski,
- **četvrtak**: bez skupa,
- **petak, 6. studenoga**: Pazin, hotel Lovac,
- **subota, 7. studenoga**: Buje, velika vijećnica Pučkog otvorenog učilišta Buje,
- **utorak, 10. studenoga**: Valpovo, Vila Valpovo,
- **srijeda, 11. studenoga**: Nova Gradiška, Centar kompetencija Nova Gradiška,
- **četvrtak, 12. studenoga**: Bjelovar, Tehnološki park Bjelovar,
- **petak, 13. studenoga**: Samobor, hotel Lavica.

Na trenutak prekida najavu kako bi provjerio raspored, a zatim pojašnjava da je **duhovna obnova u Pazinu, koja se očekivala, odgođena**. Termin u Pazinu zato koristi za promociju knjige i predstavljanje inicijative. Za Buje objašnjava da je skup najprije htio održati u Umagu, ali u kratkom roku ondje nije dobio prostor. Stanovnike Umaga podsjeća da su Buje udaljene tek desetak kilometara.

Voditelj više puta moli gledatelje iz Istre i ostalih spomenutih mjesta da **preuzmu bannere**, podijele ih na društvenim mrežama ili pošalju snimku zaslona u svoje WhatsApp grupe, kako bi na skupove došlo što više ljudi. Bannere najavljuje na Facebook stranici inicijative.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak najavljuje molitvene susrete, promociju knjige i građansku inicijativu, ali ne iznosi dovoljno teološkog sadržaja da bi se procijenila vjernost njezinih poruka katoličkom nauku. U samim najavama nema jasnog proturječja s vjerom, no njihova usklađenost ovisi o sadržaju inicijative i načinu na koji se domoljublje povezuje s kršćanskim svjedočenjem.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska se vjera može svjedočiti i u svakodnevnom društvenom okruženju, ali domoljubna djelatnost ne bi smjela zamijeniti evanđeosko poslanje niti se predstavljati kao uvjet vjernosti Crkvi. U ovom sažetku nema dovoljno podataka da bi se utvrdilo kako inicijativa Ora et Labora te odnose razumije; katolički je ideal svjedočiti vjeru dosljednim životom u vlastitoj sredini.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage announces prayer meetings, a book promotion, and a civic initiative, but does not present sufficient theological content to evaluate the fidelity of its messages to Catholic doctrine. In the announcements themselves there is no clear contradiction with the faith, but their alignment depends on the content of the initiative and the way in which patriotism is linked with Christian witness.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian faith can also be witnessed in daily social surroundings, but patriotic activity should not replace evangelical mission nor be presented as a condition of fidelity to the Church. In this summary there is not enough data to determine how the Ora et Labora initiative understands those relationships; the Catholic ideal is to witness to faith through a consistent life in one's own environment.

sections.subtitle_en: Promotions of the book "Jesus the Leader" and presentation of the initiative across cities
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar announces the schedule of book promotions and presentations of the patriotic initiative
sections.content_en:
After the interpretation, Grebenar announces a series of gatherings where he presents the book **"Jesus the Leader"** and the **patriotic initiative Ora et Labora**. Each gathering begins **at 7 p.m. with prayer**, followed by the book promotion and presentation of the initiative.

The schedule he presents:

- **Tuesday, November 3**: Solin, Hotel President Solin,
- **Wednesday, November 4**: Imotski, Public Open University Imotski,
- **Thursday**: no gathering,

For a moment he interrupts the announcement to check the schedule, and then clarifies that the **spiritual renewal in Pazin, which was expected, has been postponed**. The date in Pazin is therefore used for the book promotion and presentation of the initiative. Regarding Buje, he explains that he initially wanted to hold the gathering in Umag, but could not obtain a venue there on short notice. He reminds residents of Umag that Buje is only about ten kilometers away.

The host repeatedly asks viewers from Istria and the other mentioned places to **download banners**, share them on social networks, or send a screenshot into their WhatsApp groups, so that as many people as possible come to the gatherings. He announces the banners on the initiative's Facebook page.

sections.subtitle: Poziv na članstvo i donacije te blagoslov za kraj
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva na učlanjenje u inicijativu Ora et Labora uz prikaz kontakt-brojeva
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim poziva gledatelje da postanu **članovi domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora**. Postupak opisuje korak po korak:

1. na web-stranici diol.hr ispuni se prijavni obrazac,
2. nakon slanja prijave stiže potvrda da je prijava zaprimljena,
3. zatim stiže još jedna e-poruka s obaviješću o primanju u članstvo.

Na ekranu su prikazani **brojevi mobitela za Hrvatsku i Europsku uniju te za BiH**, na koje se može zatražiti pomoć oko prijave, plaćanja članarine ili donacije.

Upućuje i poziv na **financijsku potporu inicijativi**. Zahvaljuje svima koji su već donirali i otvorili trajni nalog. Neki daju desetinu, a neki, kako kaže, „dobiju poticaj od Gospodina“ da uplate određeni iznos. „Mi znamo što ćemo s tim sredstvima. Bogu na slavu“, ističe.

Na kraju napominje da toga dana neće stići pročitati svjedočanstva, nego će to učiniti sljedećih dana. Emisiju zaključuje blagoslovom: „Neka se sveta Mati sa svojim Sinom i svetim Josipom udostoji blagoslov svoj nam dati.“ Dodaje da se **kupnjom prve, druge i treće knjige „Isus lider“** osobno njemu pomaže dovršiti projekt **Međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira u Međugorju**. Gledatelje poziva da svaki dan prate Ora et Labora te završava riječima: „Neka je sve na veću slavu Božju.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na članstvo i dobrovoljne donacije sam po sebi nije u sukobu s katoličkim naukom, a završni zaziv Marije i svetoga Josipa može se razumjeti kao molba za njihov zagovor. Ipak, formulacija o tome da Gospodin neke potiče na određeni iznos traži oprez: iz sažetka se ne vidi tvrdi li se samo osobno iskustvo ili se stvara dojam da je takav novčani doprinos Božji zahtjev za druge.
concerns: Izraz o poticaju od Gospodina za uplatu određenog iznosa trebalo bi jasno predstaviti kao osobno razlučivanje, a ne kao opću Božju zapovijed ili obvezu vjernika.
Zaziv da Marija sa svojim Sinom i sveti Josip daju blagoslov teološki je najjasniji ako se razumije kao molba za njihov zagovor, a ne kao pripisivanje njima izvora božanskog blagoslova.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni je jezik pobožnosti prema Mariji usmjeren na njezinu molitvenu pratnju i zagovor; Ivan Pavao II. govori o povjeravanju Mariji kako bi svojim molitvama pratila određeno djelo. Zato završni zaziv može biti katolički prikladan ako se razumije u tom smislu, dok bi kod financijskih poziva bilo korisno jasno razlikovati slobodnu donaciju od vjerske dužnosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call for membership and voluntary donations is not in itself in conflict with Catholic doctrine, and the concluding invocation of Mary and Saint Joseph can be understood as a petition for their intercession. Still, the formulation about the Lord prompting some to a specific amount requires caution: from the summary it is not evident whether only personal experience is claimed or whether the impression is created that such a monetary contribution is God's demand for others.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Ecclesial language of devotion to Mary is directed toward her prayerful accompaniment and intercession; John Paul II speaks of entrusting to Mary so that she may accompany a specific work with her prayers. Therefore, the concluding invocation can be Catholically appropriate if understood in that sense, while with financial appeals it would be useful to distinguish clearly between a free donation and a religious duty.
concerns_en: The phrase about a prompt from the Lord to pay a specific amount should be clearly presented as personal discernment, and not as a general command of God or obligation of the faithful.

The invocation asking Mary with her Son and Saint Joseph to bestow a blessing is theologically clearest if understood as a petition for their intercession, rather than as attributing to them the source of divine blessing.

sections.subtitle_en: Call for membership and donations, and blessing at the end
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host calls for joining the Ora et Labora initiative with a display of contact numbers
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then invites viewers to become **members of the patriotic initiative Ora et Labora**. He describes the procedure step by step:

1. fill out the application form on the website diol.hr,
2. after submitting the application, a confirmation arrives that the application has been received,
3. then another email arrives notifying of admission into membership.

Displayed on the screen are **mobile phone numbers for Croatia and the European Union, and for Bosnia and Herzegovina**, where one can request help with registration, payment of membership fees, or donations.

He also extends an invitation for **financial support to the initiative**. He thanks everyone who has already donated and set up a standing order. Some give a tithe, while some, as he says, "receive a prompting from the Lord" to pay a certain amount. "We know what we will do with those funds. To God's glory," he emphasizes.

At the end, he notes that he will not have time to read testimonies that day, but will do so in the following days. He concludes the show with a blessing: "May the Holy Mother with her Son and Saint Joseph deign to grant us their blessing." He adds that by **purchasing the first, second, and third book "Jesus the Leader"**, people personally help him complete the project of the **Queen of Peace International Education Center in Međugorje**. He invites viewers to follow Ora et Labora every day and concludes with the words: "May all be to the greater glory of God."
